correctness.rationale: Explicit ratio-to-Jacobi normalization uses first edge (3/2)^(s/2) and satisfies the published s=1 Bergman test. Schur complement above a strict tail norm threshold reduces the infinite spectrum to one scalar equation; bipartite Neumann expansion yields the stated ordered four terms and a uniform O((512/729)^s) remainder. Exact 2- and 3-coordinate principal compressions prove the restricted radii and sharp difference; resolvent bounds prove eigenvector localization. The isolated rank and error calculation are analytic; finite numerical checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The radius is the exact extremal zero-free invariant posed for negative Dirichlet spaces. This proves its sharp large-negative-exponent leading constant (doubling the cited general lower bound), separates geometrically significant exponential corrections from successive Jacobi edges, quantifies the precise generator-degree cost within first-degree optimal approximants, and localizes extremizers. It is a mathematically motivated partial resolution, not an arbitrary finite slice.
